item.title: 报春鸟 / Spring R0bins
item.description: Boris was found dead in his bed. The room had been turned over: a computer swept to the floor, a power cord torn loose, books ripped to pieces. The air carried a wet earthy smell. He lay there like a malaria patient, wrapped tight in thick blankets in the late spring, face turned toward the dim grey light out of the window. From his mouth and nostrils poured flowers — daffodils, daisies, tulips, ranunculi, violets.

item.title: 关于黄桃的战争 / The Great Peach War
item.description: The supermarket was blasting New Year music. Three people formed a triangle around a shopping cart piled with fruit, vegetables, and red couplets, staring each other down. Between them sat the last can of yellow peaches. The first woman was small and elderly. She wore a pink floral padded coat, with grey corduroy sleeve covers guarding her wrists. Short grey hair lay neatly behind her gleaming gold earrings. Her short legs were planted wide and steady, and her narrowed eyes shone with a fierce light that showed no sign of yielding.
